updates.description_en: Daitokuji Temple is the largest temple in the north of Kyoto, which conveys the splendid Zen style of Mt. Otokokushi. Since the opening of the mountain in 1326, the famous monks representing the times have been developed by the Emperor, Shogunate, and Chirikyu. In some cases, Emperor Goji praises Daitoku-dera as the “Zenen-en” and gives the light as a Zen-en. In 2026, the opening of Daitoku-ji Temple was built in the 700th year, and the opening of the exhibition is the first time ever in Tokyo. The temple treasures of Daitoku-ji temple, including the pagoda and Daitoku-ji temples, will be revealed.

updates.title_en: ICC   2026
updates.description_en: ICC、 is an exhibition that aims to create diverse expressions in modern media environments, including media and art works. The ICC開催 will be held from FY2006 to FY2021. This year’s ICC、2026 will consider the relationship between history, technology and media. In today’s media environment, the development of AI technology that generates information has been generated and distributed at unprecedented speed and scale. In that case, the information we interact is selected and re編成ed by the algorithm. Under these information environments, the framework itself is changing what is recorded and shared. History and memories can be updated in real time, and sometimes rewritten under political and economic dynamics. In this exhibition, we focus on the relationship between history, technology and media, and think about how they have been involved in the formation of history and memories, and also think about the act of “remaining/remaining”. We will introduce works that can be read from various perspectives such as sorting and elimination in recording media, distribution of images in the digital environment, the mechanics of working there, and the way of communication spilled from the framework of perception after Western modern. It also includes works that bring new perspectives on the inheritance of memories, even if not directly referred to history. Through these works, the relationship between media and history is multifaceted. Through the question of what is left and how to receive the left, the exhibition will re-examine the history and memory.
updates.description_zh: ICC,是一個旨在在包括媒體和藝術作品在內的現代媒體環境中創造多種表現形式的展覽. 國際協調委員會將於2006財政年度至2021財政年度舉行。 今年的ICC(2026)將審議歷史、技術和媒體之間的關係。 在今天的媒體環境中,生成資訊的AI技術的發展已經以前所未有的速度和規模產生和發行. 在這種情況下,我們互動的資訊被演算法選中並重新使用。 在這些資訊環境中,框架本身正在改變記錄和共享的內容。 歷史和記憶可以實時更新,有時在政治和經濟動態下重寫. 在這次展覽中,我們著重探討歷史、技術和媒體之間的關係,思考它們如何參與歷史和記憶的形成,並思考“保留/保留”的行為。 我們將介紹能夠從各種角度閱讀的作品,如在錄製媒體中進行分類和消除,在數字環境中傳播影象,在那裡工作的機械,以及西方現代之後從認知框架溢位的傳播方式. 它還包括給記憶的繼承帶來新視角的作品,即使沒有直接提及歷史. 透過這些作品,媒體與歷史的關係是多方面的. 展會透過"左傳"和"如何接收左傳"的問題,重新審視歷史和記憶.

updates.title_en: MAM Screen 023: Josh Klein
updates.description_en: Recall and Storage: Gasoline (2023) and Recall and Storage: Cigarette (2023) All of them will be released for the first time in Japan. The two works re作品は the system itself that has been implemented for a long time, such as mining, imperialism, and industrialization of resources at the base of climate crisis. The title of both works refers to the experimental method "CO2 recovery and storage" which extracts carbon dioxide in the atmosphere and stores underground as a technical solution to climate crisis. Klein throws a question of what happens when trying to remove and enclose it, such as "destructive atmosphere" of social, political and historical mechanisms that cannot be easily changed. It is a core industry such as petroleum, tobacco, sugar, cotton, etc. that the collection and storage are focused. The production and distribution of these products has been the leading part of the United States as a military, economic and cultural empire. These materials also recall 奴隷ence in the historical origin of climate change—a slave of people living in Africa and land seizures of indigenous people. In the two works of this exhibition, petroleum and tobacco become a symbol of condensing its long history through small-controlled combustion.

updates.title_en: "The 100th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Metropolitan Art Museum"
updates.description_en: The Tokyo Metropolitan Museum of Art opened in 1926 in Ueno. The establishment of the museum was realized by Keitaro Sato, a coal company from Kitakyushu, donated 1 million yen as a museum construction fund. After the opening of the museum, he played a role as a venue for the presentation of the artist group, and sometimes became a stage for the exhibition of the legendary avant-garde art, and also became a venue for many exhibitions 。 by Taizai Meie. In addition, we have been pioneering activities to deepen understanding of art, such as art lectures and library, and have provided various places for citizen participation. The museum, like a square where art creators and recipients cross, has been aimed at becoming a place of creativity and coexistence in the past 100 years. The 100th anniversary of the opening of the museum will be held on the stage of the Tokyo Metropolitan Art Museum. The museum will look back on the history of the museum by focusing on the activities and the people who visit it. We hope that you will be able to recons  the history and role of the first public museum in Japan with valuable materials centered on our archives.

Taizai Meie. 此外,我們一直在開展開拓性活動,加深對藝術的理解,如藝術講座和圖書館,併為公民參與提供了各種場所。 博物館就像藝術創作者和接受者交叉的廣場一樣,在過去100年中一直致力於成為創造力和共存的地方. 博物館開館100週年會在東京都大都會藝術博物館舞臺上舉行. 博物館將回顧博物館歷史,關注活動及參觀者. 我們希望你們能夠重新審視日本第一家公共博物館的歷史和作用,以我們檔案為中心提供寶貴的材料。

updates.description_zh: "幾乎,天空:Atsushi Aoki + Richard Tuttle"試圖移除迄今為止如何使用展覽室的框架,使整個有機空間. 為此,我們在畫廊三樓的“Terada Kotaro紀念畫廊”舉辦了一個收藏展覽。 此外,會場外的博物館商店也改為展覽室,商店也遷至展覽室的臥鋪. 我們收藏的寺田藏品由東京歌劇院城大樓聯合運營商Atsushi Terada收藏和捐贈。 在展覽"幾乎是空的"中,藏品展拜仁青木將連線到展覽上. 這次青木從收藏中選擇. 它是一座以野外或廣闊的天空為背景的大型建築如柱子,塔樓,工廠,城堡和氣球的畫家. 古典,當代和現代建築的建築風格是從直線建築史上展開的,給人留下了永恆的印象. 似乎畫中總是沒有人類的外表,只有人類消失後站起來的遺蹟. 這幅美麗的畫的建築 讓你產生了一種奇怪的感覺 儘管你從未見過它 諾瑪塔的建築風格與"幾乎是天空"的展覽空間和諧地繪製. 在繪畫和展覽空間中獨立的柱子不支援,在天空升起的氣球重疊成從天花板上懸掛的一籃子的半球. 雖然繪畫的建築尚存,但展覽空間在光照下每天改變一次. 同時,時空矛盾也會看清面貌.

updates.description_en: The Tokyo Photographic Art Museum will hold "Yururi Island 1950–2026" from December 1, 2026 (Tuesday) to January 17, 2027 (Sunday). Atsushi。da, a photographer, is a writer who has consistently faced the fundamental theme of living with his own existence and life and death. The foundation of the production is a quiet passion in one subject, and there is a manazushi that continues to be seen throughout the year. This exhibition is a collection of creative activities in Yurli Island, which is located on the offshore of Nemuro Peninsula. In addition to the works and related videos of "The Horses of Yururi Island" (Blue Palace), which were published in 2025, we will also release a new work that captures the appearance of two remaining horses. Atsushi da was born in Hokkaido, and moved from Osaka University of Arts to Tokyo Poly  University. In 2008, he received the 33rd Kimura Ihei photo award at the photo book "I am" (Akaya). After that, he has released his works with the first winner ataraxia, the world, and the MOTHER. The horses that have been chasing for many years are the appearance of uninhabited islands that are prohibited on land. In Yurli Island, 8 km of the surrounding area, residents of the northern territory, who followed their hometown after the war, moved their horses from 1950 as a work force for kelp fishing. However, only horses are left when people leave the island. On the other hand, the island was designated as a national bird protection zone in order to protect precious nature such as sea birds such as Etoguaca, and landed substantially in the early 1980s. Thus, only lews will survive on the island of zero residents. In 2008,島da received the Kimura Ihei photo award, he was very interested in this island. Since 2011, we have been allowed to take photos on the island. This is the beginning of the history of 幻pathies with horses who live in the "phantom island" over a long period of time, far beyond the expectations of田da himself. Since only female, the flock is fate that disappears.カメラda had a single島 on the island of陸. In April of the year 15 years, ten horses at the start of shooting have been reduced to two horses.インタビューda has interviewed and investigated the former residents. Prior to the previous photo book "Horse of the island of Yurli", he has also published works such as photo-polterage "Epitaf: Ghost Island, Yurli's Light Ruins" (inpress). Due to this activity, the existence of Yurli Island and the horses living there has become many people. A phantom horse that embodies the theme of theの写真da of life and death. This exhibition is an exhibition that touches the path of the quiet passion of photographers who have continued to pursue their appearance. [Re  Event] 1. updates.title_en: Miha Tada: Light,  and Yure
updates.description_en: The Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo will hold a large-scale solo exhibition of Miha Tada (1924–2014), which was active as an abstract s、ptor and modeling artist in postwar Japan. With over 200 sculptures in life and 500 architectural works, Tada has been working in various places in the city, including parks, stations, city halls, hotels and theaters. A wide variety of expressions, such as stainless steel sculptures that stretch toward the sky, glass and acrylic sculptures that are comfortable with natural landscapes, or “light walls” that incorporate colorful light. Tada is one of the pioneering artists who actively incorporate industrial materials and processing technologies that are popular in the background of the advanced economic growth. In  surfaces that do not feel the traces of production, we incorporate organic elements such as light reflection, transmission, refractiveness, and swaying, and we have created a model that changes expressions according to the surrounding environment and the movement of viewers. These attempts are positioned in post-war abstract formulation, which is aimed at the relationship between space and the environment, away from the norms of academic elephant sculptures that focus on mass and stability. In particular, Tada has built its own position in the tide of the same era by working in the space itself while crossing art, product design, interior and architecture. These work was realized by sharp sensitivity and心 into new materials and technologies, as well as a solid relationship of trust with collaborators. At the bottom of this site, we explore the “second nature” as a beauty that can only be created by humans. In this exhibition, we will exhibit about 70 works of lighting including chandeliers, which are called “photography” by the artist, and archive materials such as architectural parts, photos, and sketches.
updates.description_zh: 當代東京藝術博物館將舉辦一個大型的獨奏展,展出Miha Tada(1924–2014),該展出在戰後的日本作為抽象的雕塑者和模特藝術家活躍. 塔達擁有200多件生活雕塑和500多件建築作品,一直在市內各地工作,包括公園,車站,市政廳,酒店和劇院. 各種各樣的表達方式,例如向天空伸展的不鏽鋼雕塑、與自然景觀相適應的玻璃和丙烯雕塑,或包含多彩光的“光牆”。 塔達是開拓性藝術家之一,積極吸收先進經濟增長背景下流行的工業材料和加工技術. 在不感受生產痕跡的表面,我們吸收了光反射,傳播,折射,搖晃等有機元素,我們創造了一種模型,根據周圍環境和觀眾運動來改變表達方式. 這些嘗試定位於戰後抽象的提法中,以空間與環境的關係為目標,遠離注重質量和穩定性的學術大象雕塑規範. 特別是,塔達在穿越藝術,產品設計,內飾和建築的同時,透過在空間本身工作,在同一個時代的潮流中建立了自己的地位. 這些工作是透過敏銳的敏感性和對新材料和技術的集中化以及與合作者的牢固信任關係來實現的。 在這個站點的底部,我們探索“第二自然”是一種只有人類才能創造的美麗。 在這個展覽中,我們將展出大約70件照明作品,包括藝術家稱之為“攝影”的吊燈,以及建築部件、照片和草圖等檔案材料。

updates.description_en: The British Museum in London opened in 1753. The museum’s collection of Japanese art is well known as one of the most comprehensive in overseas. Since the latter half of the 19th century, Japonism has been fasc。 by the culture of foreign countries and Japan, separating the sea. The connections built by numerous collectives and curators extend beyond borders and eras, and are passed down to today. In this exhibition, we will introduce the works carefully selected by eight representative Ukiyo-e-shi, such as the Edo period屏 screen, hanging scroll, picture scroll, Utamaro, Ka楽, Hokusai, Hiroshige, etc. from the collection of the four million points. In addition, the museum plays a role in the collection, research, and conservation of Japanese art by lighting the background of recent research results and collection. In addition to reflecting the history of international cultural exchange, it will be an opportunity to interact with the famous Japanese art that has been passed down to the British Museum and with us who live today.
updates.description_zh: 倫敦大英博物館於1753年開幕. 博物館收藏的日本藝術被譽為海外最全面的藝術之一. 自19世紀後半葉以來,日本主義因外國和日本的文化而變得法西斯化,隔海相望. 許多集體和館長建立的聯絡超越了國界和時代,直到今天。 在這次展覽中,我們將從四百萬分收藏品中,介紹八位代表烏基堯-e-shi精心挑選的作品,如江戶時期的屏風,掛卷,圖片卷軸,烏塔馬羅,卡楽,浩澤,弘志等. 此外,該博物館透過點亮近期研究成果和藏品的背景,在日本藝術的收藏,研究和儲存中扮演了角色. 除了反映國際文化交流的歷史外,它還將是一個與日本著名藝術進行交流的機會,這些藝術已經傳到大英博物館,並與今天的我們生活在一起.

updates.description_en: Claude Monet, born in 1840, became the world as a central painter of the派ionist, with the first派ionist exhibition in 1874. Odiron Rudon, born in the same year as Monet, debuted in the book “Dreams” (1879). Although it was unfamiliar for the late departure of 39 years old, it became the world gradually as a result of being introduced in the novel "Sakashima" (1884) of Yusumansu. This is a two-man painter who expressed the inner world to Monet who depicts the changes in the outer world, and the difference has been highlighted, but as a painter living in the same era, the common point is also seen. In 1868, Ludon had a critic of Monet and Pisaro, which was earlier than the派ionist exhibition, and it was counted as one of the critics who were interested in the派ionist. Both Monet and Ludon lived in the same age as the former painter, such as Koro and others, and they wanted to express cutting edge at that time. The Mitsubishi Ichigokan Art Museum has two works: Rudon and Monet. This year marks the 110th anniversary of the death of Monet in 100 years, the exhibition focuses on the same era of Monet and Ludon, with 16 other painters added works of the Mitsubishi Ichigokan Museum of Art.

updates.title_en: "MOT Collection: I'm looking at some light."
updates.description_en: The Tokyo Metropolitan Museum of Contemporary Art holds approximately 6,100 works mainly from postwar art. "MOT Collection" is an exhibition that introduces the collections of these works in various ways. In this period, we will constitute a new collection of works, focusing on light and time, titled "I have seen some light now". The light emitted over thousands of years from the stars of far away, the sunshine, the moonlight, the light of the lights, the light of the lights that shine around, the light of the fireflies. “Seeing/watching/watching” will also lead to the emergence of the time and time of the past. The “now” we live will be created by overlapping and co ation of time passed down from the past with light. In this exhibition, we will try to think about the severity by looking at the past that is wrapped in the present time through works such as Mami Osemura, Koo Tsuchiya, Arisa Kumagaya, and Nario Toya.
updates.description_zh: 東京都市當代博物館 藝術收藏了約6100部作品,主要來自戰後藝術. "MOT收藏"是一個以各種方式介紹這些作品的收藏的展覽. 在這段時間裡,我們將組成新的作品集,側重於光和時間,題為"我已經看到了一些光". 遠方的恆星,陽光,月光,光芒,光芒四射的光芒,螢火蟲的光芒,千百年來發出的光芒. “看/看/看”還會導致過去的時間和時間的出現。 我們所生活的“現在”將因時間的重疊和相互交織而產生。 在這場展覽中,我們將透過Mami Osemura、Koo Tsushiya、Arisa Kumagaya和Nario Toya等作品來審視當前所包裹的過去,來思考其嚴重程度。

updates.title_en: “Takehisa Yumeji: An Expression to Create the Era”
updates.description_en: Yuji Takehisa (1884-19。 was an artist,ジャーナリスト, journalist, designer, and illustrator. It is known as a symbol of Taisho Romans by the female statue called "Yumeji" and the retro modern design. Yumeji’s work, which depicts the customs of the same era, has spread to the public through magazines, picture books, exhibitions, etc. In addition, the design of daily necessities that color everyday life, making books and magazines for children, writing lyrics of the epidemic song "Yoyois" and sketches and words that reflected the Great Kanto Earthquake, etc. This exhibition is a collection of Japanese paintings, oil paintings, sketches, various designs, scrapbooks, and more. Beyond the boundaries of art, take a look at the times, create trends, and focus on expressions loved by people.
updates.description_zh: Takehisa Yuji(1884-19.)是一位藝術家,QQ,記者,設計師,插畫家. 它被女神雕像稱為"尤梅吉"(Yumeji)和復古的現代設計稱為"大修羅馬人的象徵". 尤梅吉的作品描繪了同一時代的風俗習慣,透過雜誌,圖片圖書,展覽等方式向公眾傳播. 此外,還設計了色彩日常生活的日常必需品,為兒童製作書籍和雜誌,為疫情歌曲"Yoyois"譜寫歌詞,以及反映關東大地震的草圖和文字等. 本次展覽收藏了日本畫,油畫,素描,各種設計,剪貼畫等等. 超越藝術的界限,看一看時代,創造趨勢,注重人們所喜愛的表達方式.

updates.title_en: “Mako Idemitsu – Self-development of a filmmaker”
updates.title_zh: “Mako 同上-電影製片人的自我發展”
updates.description_en: Masako Idemitsu (1940–) is a pioneer of experimental films and video art in Japan. In the 1960s, he started his work in the U.S., and released films and video works based on the theme of the relationship between women, families, media and society. In particular, in the 1970s and later video works, the theme of mothers, children, couples, and women's social roles is drawn from a unique perspective. In recent years, it has been attracting attention to its practice in the increasing international discussion of gender and body. This exhibition is a large retrospective exhibition that reflects the full view of the creative activities of Idemitsu, including the first public work. We will introduce all the artworks collected at the museum through exhibitions and screenings. * “What a woman made” in this exhibition title uses the title of the first video work (1973), which determines the evaluation of the filmmaker Masako Idemitsu.
updates.description_zh: Masako Idejitsu(1940年-)是日本實驗電影和錄影藝術的先驅. 1960年代,他開始在美國工作,發行了以婦女,家庭,媒體和社會的關係為主題的電影和影視作品. 特別是在1970年代和後來的影視作品中,母親,子女,夫婦的主題,以及女性的社會角色都是從獨特的視角來借鑑的. 近年來,它一直在吸引人們注意它在國際上越來越多地討論性別和身體問題方面的做法。 這次展覽是大型的回顧展覽,反映了包括第一部公共作品在內的Idebitsu的創作活動的全景. 我們將透過展覽和放映介紹博物館收藏的所有藝術品。 * 本展覽標題中的“婦女製造的東西”使用了第一部錄影作品的標題(1973年),這決定了對電影製片人Masako Ideritsu的評價。

updates.title_en: "Tokyo Pack" and its Period + Special Exhibition」ten Kitazawa's "Kids No Tomo"
updates.title_zh: "東京包"及其時期+特別展覽"滕北澤"孩子無託莫".
updates.description_en: Tokyo Pack was born in 1905 as Japan’s first full-color manga magazine using a stone-block print. It was popular with colorful andモアorous sashimi comics, and it conveyed the life of the society from time to time such as politics, international situations, fashion, and living. This magazine was published in   (Showa16) while repeating prohibition and resting. In this exhibition, we will introduce 96 original paintings of the 3rd and 4th Tokyo Pack, which were produced from the 1920s to the 30s. The work was drawn from the reconstruction period after the Great Kanto Earthquake to the World War. The people who live every day, while being conf  by changes in society, and having anxiousness, will become more important to us than ever. The sashimi has reflected the social conflicts and the real sound of people, and it has always been sharp, and, sometimes, reflected in the era. From the "Tokyo Pack" page, you can feel the feelings and the atmosphere of the people of the time and society that are not visible only by the textbook of history. In addition, this year is the 150th anniversary of the birth of東京ten Kitazawa, which is the first professional manga artist in Japan. In line with this, we will exhibit the original picture of "Kids Noyu" (published by Noyusha Co., Ltd.) for children, which Kitazawa was the chief painter. You will be able to see the charm of ten Kitazawa different from the sashimi manga from the works full of familiarity drawn for children. Through the work of “Tokyo Pack” and。ten Kitazawa, the people of 100 years ago will come to life from the viewpoint of the present.
updates.description_zh: "東京包"誕生於1905年,是日本第一本使用石塊印刷的全綵漫畫雜誌. 這部作品以色彩鮮豔的莎士比亞漫畫為熱門,不時傳達了政治,國際形勢,時尚,生活等社會生活. 該雜誌發表於(Sshowa16),同時重複禁止和休息. 在這次展覽中,我們將介紹從1920年代到30年代製作的三四東京包的96幅原畫. 工程取材自關東大地震後的重建時期到世界大戰. 每天活下來的人,雖然被社會的變化所迷惑,並且焦慮不安,對我們來說,將變得比以往任何時候都更加重要. 沙希米反映了社會矛盾和人們的真實聲音,始終是尖銳的,有時也反映於時代. 從"東京包"的一頁,可以感受到當時和社會上人們的感情和氣氛,這些感情和氣氛僅靠歷史教科書是看不到的. 此外,今年是北澤東京誕辰150週年,是日本第一位專業漫畫藝術家. 據此,我們將展出"野玉童"(由野玉沙股份有限公司出版)的原畫,以北澤為首席畫家. 你會看到十隻北澤的魅力 不同於畫像和畫像 透過《東京包》和《北澤》的工作,100年前的人民將從現在的角度復活。

updates.description_en: Renamed the National Museum of Modern Art, Tokyo in 1967. The museum was born as the first National Art Museum in Japan. It was not a new building, but the former Nissei Head Office Building of Tokyo and Kyobashi was renovated. The National Museum of Modern Art was built as a “movable museum” to reconstruct cultural reconstruction after the war. Hasegawa Saburo (1906–1957), a pioneer of abstract art in Japan, plays an important role in the exhibition “幻想 and Fantasy” (1953) and “Japan-U.S. 。 Art Exhibition (。)” held in方針 with the museum’s policy. Hasegawa has been positioned not only as a painter, but also as a critic and thinker, as it symbolizes "art" and "theory". In this section, I will focus on the aspects of the curator. Through the 120th anniversary of the birth of this year, the works of Hasegawa and the works of related artists, the works of the exhibition, and the introduction of lifelong writing activities, we will continue to be a comprehensive artist. I would like to express my deep app。。 to all of the people involved in this exhibition, including the Konan Gakuen Hasegawa Saburo Memorial Gallery.
updates.description_zh: 1967年改名為東京國立現代藝術博物館. 該博物館誕生於日本第一家國家藝術博物館. 雖然不是新建的建築,但原東京和京橋的尼世總公司大樓進行了翻修. 國家現代藝術博物館是作為戰後重建文化重建的"可移動博物館"建成的. 長谷川·薩布羅(1906年-1957年)是日本抽象藝術的先驅,在日本博物館的政策下,在1953年舉辦的 " 幻想與幻想 " 和 " 日本-美國.藝術展覽(.) " 中發揮了重要作用。 長谷川不僅被定位為畫家,還被定位為評論家和思想家,因為它象徵著"藝術"和"理論". 在本節中,我將重點談談館長的方方面面。 透過今年誕辰120週年,長谷川的作品及相關藝術家的作品,展覽的作品,以及終身寫作活動的引進,我們將繼續成為綜合性的藝術家. 我要向參與這次展覽的所有人表示深切的感謝,包括Konan Gakuen Hasegawa Saburo紀念畫廊。

By looking at the work as a “food” approach, there is a variety of notices that are connected to memories and people related to the meal, and the question of the social problems such as the environment, aging, orphanage that we are currently in is born. This exhibition is composed of four sections: Shinzo Shimao, Satoka Noguchi, Tokuko Shioda, Mikiko Hara, Tomoko Kawauchi, Kazutaka Narahara, Michitaka。, Taketani, Takashi Miyamoto, Hiromi Miyazaki, Hiromi Tsuchida, Asako Narahashi, Yu Iwai, and Tatsumi Orimoto. In this exhibition, the works of Buddhist art, one of the pillars of the collection of the museum, are composed of the six chapters: the Sutra and Buddhism Con、, the Buddha and His Disciples, the Ko、 Pure Land and Hell, the Hokakyo Faith, the Fugen Bodhisattva, the Shibukyo, and the Jinbutsukai. Nostalgia’s dismantlement is a work that combines archive, print, oil painting, acrylic paint, rope and metal equipment. The painting called “Mooy Indy”, which draws a nostalgic landscape that harmonizes people and nature, reveals how the colonial 平ence and imbalances have been hidden. In the same colonial rule, the space at the time (in 2024) and the latest film Sora Farta (in 2025), the eyes of the past distorted the historical facts, and the nostalgia of the dictation and the colonial administration, Ksuno is critically questioned.

updates.title_en: “MAM Research 012: Diaポ Memory – Collian Artists that Live beyond boundaries”
updates.title_zh: “MAM 研究 012: DiaQQ 記憶 — — 超越國界的科利安藝術家”
updates.description_en: People and descendants who moved to foreign countries and settled in their country are called Diaポ. Now, immigrants and refugees in all parts of the world are increasing, and the rebounds in multiculturalism and the waves of nationalism are increasing, and the existence of such people has never been sharp. In South Korea, especially in neighboring countries, many dearポora have been praised in Asia due to the history of colonial control, Korean war, dictation and democracy, rapid economic development and globalization. However, the existence of "Corrian Diaポra" is often spoken in a fixed framework called national and ethnicity, and its diversity and liquidity were not fully recognized. In this exhibition, we will follow the trajectory of Korean Diaポra in the 20th and 21st century through works and related materials of three artists who passed from Korea to another country or have roots. Kwak Insik (born 1919 in Daegu, South Korea, 1988 in Tokyo), Sung Hyunsuk (born 1952 in South Korea, Germany, Hamburg), and South Korea, Alexander Wugai (born 1978 inハンブルク Kzilorda, Almaty and Seoul), respectively, have explored the intersection of national and personal memories, migration and identity conflicts, and his hometown. When you live in these different land and face the works and life history of artists created by different languages and cultures, you will see that Diポora’s experience is not just loss or disco。ation. Through the practice of three artists across multiple regions, languages, and cultures, we will rethink the memory that overlaps beyond the boundaries from a new perspective.
updates.description_zh: 遷居外國並在他們國家定居的人和後裔被稱為Diaポ. 現在,世界各地的移民和難民人數在增加,多元文化的反彈和民族主義的浪潮在增加,這種人的存在從未如此尖銳. 在韓國,特別是在鄰國,由於殖民控制的歷史、朝鮮戰爭、獨裁和民主、經濟的迅速發展和全球化,許多親愛的奧拉在亞洲受到讚揚。 然而,"Corrian Diaポra"的存在經常在一個稱為民族和族裔的固定框架內被說成,其多樣性和流動性也沒有得到充分的承認. 在本次展覽中,我們將透過三位藝術家的作品和相關材料,透過他們從韓國傳到另一個國家或有根基,來跟蹤20世紀和21世紀韓國的Diaポra的軌跡. Kwak Insik(1919年生於韓國大邱,1988年生於東京),Sung Hyunsuk(1952年生於韓國,德國,漢堡)和韓國,Alexander Wugai(1978年生於Kzilorda,阿拉木圖和漢城)分別探索了民族記憶和個人記憶的交匯點,移民和身份衝突,以及他的家鄉. 當你生活在這些不同的土地上,並面對不同語言和文化所創造的藝術家的作品和生活歷史時,你會看到迪尤拉的經歷不僅僅是失落或迪斯科化。 透過三位藝術家跨越多個地區,語言,文化的實踐,我們將從新的角度重新思考超越邊界的記憶。

updates.description_en: “MAM Project 035” introduces Bry Ley based in Santa Fe, New Mexico. We have created sculptures that incorporate performive elements, focusing on the materiality of ceramics and the artist’s own physicality and manual work. In the typical series, there is a work formed by the movement of the whole body such as裂ing, tearing and scratching the clay of the same weight as its own weight. In these works, the presence and experience of the body is reflected, and the strong movement and表s are expressed in a unique artistic practice that combines the characteristics of soil and physical activity. In this exhibition, we will conduct research on the history of Japanese clay and ceramics, and present new works that combine the results with their own practice. A collection of works born from intimate dialogue between the earth and the body, question the relationship between our body, the earth and the existence.
updates.description_zh: “MAM Project 035”介紹Bry Ley總部位於新墨西哥州聖菲。 我們創作了包含表演元素的雕塑,其重點是陶瓷的質感以及藝術家自己的體能和體力工作. 在典型的系列中,有一部由全身運動形成的作品,如塗抹,撕裂和刮刮與自身重量相同的粘土. 在這些作品中,身體的存在和經驗得到反映,強勢運動和吊床表現為一種獨特的藝術實踐,結合了土壤和身體活動的特徵. 在這次展覽中,我們將對日本粘土和陶瓷的歷史進行研究,並介紹將成果與自己的實踐相結合的新作品. 從地球與身體之間的親密對話中誕生的作品集,質疑我們的身體,地球與存在之間的關係.

In ancient times, the textile industry, which is centered on textiles, has evolved into traditional handcrafts that have been conveyed throughout the world, but the design of printed textiles will be opened by technological innovation in the mid-20th century. In this exhibition, you will be able to listen to the charm of the exhibition from three perspectives: motifs, designers, and life. Tofukumon-in (Wako Tokugawa) is a woman whose culture has been developed for the second half of the 17th century. In her surroundings, she became the daughter of the Shogun and the emperor of the emperor, the emperor of Gosuio, Senshu, Kobori Enshu, Shoji Matsukado, and Nichiki Nomura. updates.description_zh: 1626年9月,高句麗皇帝高句麗訪問京都的尼若城堡. 9月5日的第一天,京城將是一個活躍的國度,位於天前,在皇帝的大型陵寢遊行,公館,將軍和國大名. 康永吉講述大平世界的到來,據說他孕育了新文化. 在這次展覽中,我們將主要從重現遊行隊伍的伊澤米雅·哈庫坎的藏品中回顧這一歷史繁榮. 富士門仁(英語:Wako Tokugawa)是一名女性,其文化發展於17世紀下半葉. 在她的周圍,她成為幕府和皇帝之女,高句麗,仙遊,高伯裡恩修,松下道順治,野村信一的皇帝. 在會場上,我們將看到豐富門仁的產品,成為公眾與公眾的橋樑,我們將跟隨信仰的腳步. 賓館附近有豐富門寧博紹吉寺的孔廟,江戶重建初期的神廟. 請花點時間來思考這裡的坎那加文化,傳達過去米亞那加的氣息.

updates.title_en: "Myths, Fables, Festivals: Italian courts and prints in Baroque fromネ
updates.title_zh: "神話,寓言,節日:義大利法院和巴洛克的指紋來自
updates.description_en: In Italy during theネ period, the image of the gods of Greek Roman mythology has been revived, with the rise of interest in classical ancient times and the spread of humanisticism. These statues are readable as fables under the humanistic classical interpretation, and will play a political and iconic role in the court festival. In this exhibition, the image of myths, fables, and court festivals created fromネ to Baroque, will be traced through about 50 prints from our collection. In the latter half of the 15th century, when the production of copper prints became full-scale, the statue像 from ancient gods and symbolic systems was also introduced and distributed as a theme. In the 16th century, reproductions based on Lafael’s works were produced in Rome, and printmakers such as Marcantonio Limondi are active. Many of these prints were subjected to myths and fables decoding, and were the main subject of app、。 and collectives with humanistic organs. In the same period, a wide variety of版ve prints indicating the design of residence decoration are used as visual materials for artists and craftsmen. In addition, prints played an important role in publications for court festivals. In particular, in the Medici court of Florence, the scenes of the monarch statue, emb s, myths and fables were printed, conveying the vibrancy of the splendid court culture and city, and conveying the message of monarchy to other urban courts. In this exhibition, we will introduce the world-famous image created in the intellectual and aesthetic tide of the Italian court culture, starting with the ancient statue of the early bronze prints, the reproduction prints developed in Rome and Mantova, the illustrations of decorations and crafts, and the celebrations by Jacquard painter. See how myths, fables, and festivals develop together through these works.
updates.description_zh: 在五月時期的義大利,希臘羅馬神話中的神祇形象得到了恢復,對古典古代的興趣和人文主義的傳播也隨之增加. 這些雕像在人文主義的古典詮釋下可作為寓言來閱讀,並將在宮廷節日中扮演政治和標誌性的角色. 在這場展覽中,神話、寓言和宮廷節日的畫面 將從我們收藏的50個指紋中找到。 15世紀後半葉,銅印的製作成為了全盛時期,古代神祇和象徵體系的雕像也作為主題引入和發行. 16世紀,基於拉斐爾作品的複製品在羅馬製作,馬克桑託尼奧·利蒙迪等印刷廠活躍. 這些印記中有許多都受到神話和寓言的解碼,是人文器官的應用和集體的主要課題. 在同一時期,各種表明住宅裝飾設計的版字印刷品被用作藝術家和工匠的視覺材料. 此外,印刷品在法院節的出版物中發揮了重要作用。 特別是在佛羅倫薩的美第奇宮廷,君主雕像的場景,emb s,神話和寓言被印刷,傳達了輝煌的宮廷文化和城市的活力,並向其他城市法院傳達了君主制的資訊. 在這次展覽中,我們將介紹義大利宮廷文化的智力和美學潮流中創造的世界著名形象,從早期青銅印畫的古老鵰像,羅馬和曼託瓦開發的複製印畫,裝飾和工藝的插圖,以及雅克誇德畫家的慶祝活動開始. 看神話,寓言,節日如何透過這些作品一起發展.

updates.title_zh: “長谷川清史:巴黎銅膏畫家之路”
updates.description_en: Kiyoshi Hasegawa (1891-1980), one-man-to-man-to-man after the World War I, the leading print artist in Japan, has been a lifetime in the same place. Reconstruction of the classic technique of bronze print Manière Noir, which was lost, in its own form, left a large footprint in the history of prints, and explored the technique of engraving and aquatinting. The deep spiritual world expressed by monoム has attracted many people. Hasegawa’s work had a huge impact on the Japanese print world, but his performance was still Paris. Hasegawa, whose talent as a print painter since the 1920s, was soon found in Forve’s painter Dufy and joined the “Independent Painter = Print Painter Association” in which Matisse, Picasso, and Shagir were named. Hasegawa is also working to introduce Japanese prints to French people. Hasegawa is working on an illustration book "Taketori Story" with the illustration of Engraving in Japanese classical literature. In this exhibition, the works of prints that have influenced the Hasegawa River and the works of contemporary painters who interacted in Paris, and the works of Kiyoshi Hasegawa, one of Japan’s leading works by町da City Museum of Art, will be exhibited from early to late. (approximately 130 works) In the exhibition room, you can see works that make you feel the infinite depth while drawing familiar objects. There is a deeply simmered black and soft white. When you stand before, you may not see anything. There are things that are pulled only for the look. Please look forward to seeing you at the venue.
updates.description_zh: 長谷川清之(1891年-1980年),一戰後單人畫人,日本著名印刷藝術家,一生在同一地點. 重建了青銅印刷瑪尼埃·諾伊爾的經典技術,它以自身形式失傳,在印刷史上留下了很大的足跡,並探索了雕刻和配音的技術. 由單曲表達的深刻精神世界吸引了很多人. 長谷川的作品對日本印刷界產生了巨大影響,但他的表演還是巴黎. 長谷川自20世紀20年代起就具有印刷畫家的才能,很快在福爾夫的畫家杜菲中被發現,並加入了"獨立畫家=印刷畫家協會",其中馬蒂塞,畢加索,沙吉爾被命名. 長谷川還致力於向法國人介紹日本的指紋. 長谷川正從事插圖書"竹藤故事"的創作,其插圖為日本古典文學中的Engraphy. 在這次展覽中,影響長谷川河的印刷品作品和巴黎互動的當代畫家的作品,以及日本主要作品之一的京師長谷川的作品(by 3700da City Museum of Art)將從早到晚展出. (約130件作品) 在展覽室裡,可以看到一些作品,這些作品讓你在繪製熟悉的物體的同時感受到無限的深度. 有一個深沉的黑色和軟白色。 當你站在前面,你可能什麼都看不見。 有些東西被拉出來只是為了外觀 請期待在會場見到你。

updates.title_en: “Is it on the road?”
updates.description_en: In Japan, there was a certain system and a free space called a civil society. The area seen in the temple gate and inn was also a device that accepts people and entertainment to grow culture and exchange. In modern times, "Rogami" is not completely overlapped with such historical space, but the framework of ownership and governance is ambiguous, and sometimes the resistance to the system is trying to find freedom on the road. On the other hand, on the street is not just a symbol of freedom and freedom. The logic of elimination increases comfort and unstableness. In this exhibition, we will think about the challenges of becoming more and more complex in modern times, with works that can be introduced on the road to keywords, historical things, and even speeches. The 40th anniversary of the founding of the Road Observation Society was established in 1986. The trajectory observation society formed by Akira Akasegawa and Terunobu Fujimori are activities that share "eyes" through the media, not the artistic works expressed by intention, but the situation that the city and nature have not been intentionally expressed. There was also criticism of the city which was homogenized by development. “She was a refuge” – This is the word that a perpetrator issued in the trajectory murder case in Shibuya in 2020. On the road, although ownership is vague, the public order is emphasized, and it is also a space where the subjective rules of the other collide. In the 2020 case, we found out 暴力ence that could occur when we mistake the meaning of public sex. However, there are many critical cultural practices on the road where freedom and prosperity coexist. This exhibition introduces historical materials, park playgrounds, public baths, and large street art, and explores the public nature of the streets with the keywords, from past practice to critical approaches to modern cities. Meet the arts on the street, full of criticism and喧or.

updates.description_en: Many people living in a city surrounded by artificial objects spend their days away from the earth. However, you can find new ecosystems according to changes in the environment, such as foreign species, autonomous vegetation, and organisms that coexist with concrete and plastic. As human life is the main factor of changing the natural environment, the boundary between nature and artificial is becoming more ambiguous. How can we regain connections with nature? In this exhibition, we will introduce the artists who continue to make a smooth yet supple work that will reconnect the relationship with the ever-changing natural environment. The seeds that fly to the people who are brought to the wind stretch the roots in the tra  place, and take the nutrients from there. The work as a ̶̶ species is to live without re ing even if it is antidepressed, and it stretches the roots from there and revives the texture of the earth to a。n the sense of body. Tokyo Opera City Art Gallery presents a wide variety of genres such as architecture and fashion. In this exhibition, we will introduce a series of works that interlink these efforts to capture the nature of the city.

updates.title_en: "Brilliant Modern Japanese Painting -The Beauty of Traditional Decorations"
updates.title_zh: "輝煌的現代日本繪畫——傳統裝飾的美人".
updates.description_en: The Sato Sakura Art Museum is pleased to announce the exhibition “G。ing Modern Japanese Paintings: Traditional Decorations” A world of beauty woven with gold leaf sparkling, gorgeous colors and delicate designs. This exhibition focuses on the aesthetics of "飾e" that Japanese people have developed for a long time, and introduces a number of modern Japanese paintings that are性ve. In the Japanese culture, there is a “decorational beauty” that colors the space, body, and life beautifully. The道具 screen is decorated with gold leaf and gorgeous colors, and it is an interior decoration that creates a beautiful space, while it is also a tool that blocks the wind and separates people's attention. In addition, designs and texts used in kimono, twelve pieces and traditional costumes reflect the wishes for people’s happiness and prosperity, and the spirit of pursuing beauty. In the Japanese painting, the bold and sophisticated decoration expressions representing the派in family have been inherited, and the natural and floral bird-like moon has been sublimated into brilliant beauty. In this exhibition, we will introduce works based on桜 screens, costumes, patterns, and flower bird paintings and cherry。, focusing on "tradi、 beauty", "design" and "decoration" inherited by Japanese paintings. Enjoy the world of sparkling contemporary Japanese paintings that resonate with the traditional and modern sensitivity of contemporary Japanese paintings.
updates.description_zh: 佐藤櫻花藝術博物館高興地宣佈了展覽“G. ing Modern Japan paintings:傳統裝飾”以金葉閃爍、華麗的顏色和微妙的設計編織的美麗世界。 本次展覽主要介紹日本人長期開發的"filme"的美學,並介紹一些日本現代畫作,這些畫作都令人歎為觀止. 在日本文化中,有一種“裝飾的美麗”,它以美麗的顏色描繪空間、身體和生活。 QQ螢幕以金葉和華麗的顏色裝飾,它是一種內部裝飾,創造了一個美麗的空間,同時它也是一個擋風擋風,隔離人們注意力的工具. 此外,和服中使用的圖案和文字,十二件和傳統服裝也反映了人們追求幸福和繁榮的願望,以及追求美的精神. 在日本畫中,代表百花鳥家族的大膽而精緻的裝飾表達方式被繼承,自然和花鳥般的月亮被亞化為輝煌的美麗. 在這次展覽中,我們將介紹基於QQ螢幕,服裝,圖案,以及花鳥繪畫和櫻桃的作品;重點介紹日本繪畫繼承的"輻射,美麗","設計"和"裝飾". 享受與當代日本繪畫的傳統和現代敏感性相呼應的閃爍當代日本繪畫的世界.

updates.description_en: J.M.W. Turner, the greatest painter in British painting history. His work has been highly appreciated as an experience of nature. This is a long-awaited retrospective exhibition that introduces more than 80 oil paintings and watercolor paintings from the Tate Museum in London, the world’s largest Turner Collection. In this exhibition, we will re編e the works of the Turner by theme and exhibit them in a展示 manner. In addition, we will interact with the paintings of the Turner and the viewpoint of this master’s problem consciousness to resonate with the interest of the artists of the future.
updates.description_zh: J·M·W·特納,英國畫史上最偉大的畫家. 塔納在繪畫史上開闢了新胡爾,被抽象和及時繪畫,以克服"光"和"空氣"等世界的存在. 他的作品被高度評價為自然經驗. 這是一個期待已久的回顧展覽,介紹80多幅油畫和水彩畫,它們來自倫敦塔特博物館,是世界上最大的特納收藏品. 在這次展覽中,我們將按主題重新展示特納號的作品,並以a展示的方式展出. 此外,我們將與特納的畫作和這位大師的問題意識的觀點互動,以與未來的藝術家的興趣產生共鳴。

updates.title_zh: “吉田裕也的設計:新民俗藝術運動的未來”
updates.description_en: About 100 years ago, since Setsura Yanagi advocated the philosophy of “Mingaku (Mingaku)”, the folk art movement resonated with the spirit has spread throughout Japan. “Mingei” continues to attract new interest as a keyword that can be found in the lifestyle. Yuya Yoshida (1898–1972) Yuya Yoshida worked as a producer of the folk art, from the design of new folk art to the production, distribution and sales of products. Since 1931, we have opened a院 in Tottori. We work with craftsmen in the fields of ceramics, woodworking, metalworking, dyeing, and washi. Yoshida’s “new folk art movement” is based on the beauty standard raised by Yanagi, and is designed for modern life based on traditional handwork. It has been developed together with the Tottori Mingei Museum of Art, which exhibits collections, and the Tottori Sand Dunes and Nifukaku. The tracks and essences of the new folk art movement created by Yuya Yoshida are based on about 300 works by Yoshida himself, and related materials. Please enjoy a partial reproduction exhibition of the “Old Yoshida Clinic” and “Old Yoshida Yuya Residence”.
updates.description_zh: 大約在100年前,自Setsura Yanagi提倡“明古(明古)”哲學以來,民間藝術運動與精神的共鳴已蔓延到日本各地。 “明蓋”繼續吸引新的興趣,成為生活方式中的一個關鍵詞。 吉田雄也(1898年–1972年),吉田雄也曾擔任民間藝術的製作人,從新民間藝術的設計到產品的生產,分銷和銷售. 從1931年開始,我們在託托里開業. 我們在陶瓷、木製品、金屬製品、染料和黃油等領域與工匠合作。 吉田的"新民藝術運動"以柳木升起的美容標準為基礎,以傳統手工製作為現代生活設計. 它與展出藏品的託托里·明蓋藝術博物館,託托里·沙丘和尼夫庫庫一起開發. 吉田裕也所創立的新民俗藝術運動的曲目和精髓以吉田本人的約300部作品為基礎,以及相關的材料. 請享受“老吉田診所”和“老吉田裕也住所”的部分複製展覽。

updates.description_en: Hiroshige Utagawa, who was active in the late Edo period。97-185師, is a ukiyo-e-shi who built a period with colorful flower bird paintings and landscape paintings that make you feel the transition of the four seasons. In the landscape painting, which is often synonymous with, the theme of various parts of Japan is elaborately depicted the charm of the scenery by changing the weather and time, and the people who live there. The style of this product is very fresh and easy to understand. This time, we received the 1,点 points of Ukiyo-e from the former collection of 1893-1980. Mr. Uchiyama has built a high-quality Ukiyo-e collection centered on Hiroshige Utagawa, and has extensively introduced its appeal through publications and exhibitions. This exhibition introduces three major series of landscape paintings and flower bird paintings in three stages, “Tokaido Gobuki-sanji” (First term), “Kisokaido Rokuji” (Second term), and “Hundred Views of Famous Edo” (3rd term). It is a very valuable opportunity to show all of these series at once, and to see examples both inside and outside Japan. Please enjoy the "best angles of Edo" that Hiroe took. The exhibition will be held on the following schedule. 1st period: Tuesday 29th – Sunday 25th October 2nd period: Tuesday 27th – Monday 23rd November 3rd period: Wednesday 25th – Sunday 20th December
updates.description_zh: 原活躍於江戶晚期的上川弘志(Hiroshige Utagawa). 97-18594,是一款以色彩鮮豔的花鳥繪畫和風景畫打造的時期,讓你感受到四季的過渡. 在往往與之同義的風景畫中,日本各地的主題透過改變天氣和時間來精心描繪風景的魅力,以及生活在那裡的人們. 這個產品的風格非常新鮮,易於理解. 這次,我們從1893年-1980年的原集中獲得了1,6,6,6,6,6的Ukiyo-e點. 內山先生在上川弘志(Hiroshige Utagawa)上建造了高品質的Ukiyo-e收藏品,並透過出版物和展覽廣泛介紹了它的吸引力. 這個展覽分三個階段介紹三套主要的景觀畫和花鳥畫,即“Tokaido Gobuki-sanji”(第一個任期)、“Kisokaido Rokuji”(第二個任期)和“Hundred Views of Famous Edo”(第三個任期)。 這是一個非常寶貴的機會,可以同時展示所有這些系列,並看到日本內外的例子。 請享受廣惠取的"江戶最佳角度". 展覽將按以下時間安排舉行. 第一期:第29日星期二-10月25日星期日 第二期:第27日星期二-11月23日星期一 第三期:第25日星期三-12月20日星期日
